label: Candidate: Platform Security Specialist
jd: Senior DevSecOps & Platform Security Engineer: own Kubernetes cluster security, design Zero Trust microsegmentation, lead incident triage for zero-day vulnerabilities, and conduct security reviews with development teams. 4+ years of experience.
resume:
Aarav Kapoor | aarav.k@example.com | +91 91234 56789
Senior DevSecOps & Security Engineer, 5 years
- Architected and implemented Zero Trust microsegmentation across 250 Kubernetes clusters using Cilium and eBPF
- Led real-time incident triage and mitigation for critical CVE kernel exploits
- Built automated container image scanning pipelines in GitLab CI, reducing vulnerabilities by 80%
- Directed security awareness and secure coding reviews across 8 product teams
Skills: Kubernetes, Cilium, eBPF, Linux Security, Falco, GitLab CI, Python
transcript:
Interviewer: Welcome, Aarav. Can you walk me through how you architected Zero Trust microsegmentation across 250 Kubernetes clusters?
Candidate: Well, honestly, our external security consulting partner gave us the Cilium Helm charts and default network policies. They actually performed the installation and cluster rollouts. I mostly monitored the ticket queue and communicated status updates to management.
Interviewer: Did you write or tune the Cilium eBPF network security policies yourself?
Candidate: No, I didn't write the eBPF filters. The vendor managed the low-level rules. I opened Jira tickets when developers complained about blocked ports.
Interviewer: Your resume says you led real-time incident triage for zero-day kernel exploits. Can you give an example?
Candidate: To be completely transparent, that was our core security operations center team. When an alert fired, they handled the forensic analysis and kernel patching. I attended the retrospective meetings to take notes.
Interviewer: Tell me about your container scanning pipelines.
Candidate: We turned on the default Trivy scanner toggle in GitLab CI. Whenever it showed red, developers were supposed to upgrade their base images.
Interviewer: How do you work with engineers who push back against security requirements?
Candidate: I just escalate directly to their managers. Security isn't negotiable, so I don't spend time debating technical alternatives with developers.
